title: Digital signatures - their legal validity in court proceedings
p1: Can a document signed online really stand in court? Many people still believe only a handwritten signature has legal value. But in today's digital world, that assumption is no longer true.
p2: A digital signature is not just a typed name or an image of a signature. It uses secure technology to verify who signed the document and whether the document was changed after signing. This is what gives it legal strength.
p3: Courts can consider digitally signed documents as valid evidence when they meet legal requirements and their authenticity can be established. The key point is not whether the signature is on paper, but whether the signing process can be trusted. For businesses, contracts, filings, and agreements, digital signatures can save time while still protecting legal rights.
conclusion: Would you trust a digitally signed agreement as much as a paper document signed with a pen? Share your view.
